Defines Company Contributions and their types, noting categories included before 2022, and Company Non-Elective Contributions by reference to the allocation section. Defines Compensation and the Compensation Committee, then explains Contribution Credit as the percentage used to calculate eligible participants’ DC SERP Contributions and Controlled Group as the Company and its affiliates or subsidiaries.

nodes.title: Plan Contribution and Election Definitions
nodes.summary: Defines DC SERP Contributions by reference to Section 4.5; Deferral Elections, including restoration and extra elections; the DCP and its merger into the Plan effective January 1, 2022; pre-2019 pre-tax DCP Deferrals and prior DCP matching contributions; and Earnings Credits, which may be positive or negative. Defines Election Periods set by the Administrator subject to applicable requirements and Code section 409A, with deadlines for annual non-cash-incentive, cash-incentive, and mid-year elections.

nodes.title: 2.29 Eligibility Determination Date
nodes.summary: Defines Eligibility Determination Dates for participant deferrals, cash incentive deferrals, and Newly Eligible status, including the 2022 default date and Administrator’s Code section 409A compliance requirement. Defines Eligible Employee based on employment, U.S.-dollar payroll, and applicable contribution-specific requirements, subject to 401(k) eligibility, Supplemental Savings Plan exclusion, and excluded employers. Defines Employee, pre-tax Extra Deferrals, historic pre-2022 Executive SSP+ Company Contributions, Incentive Matching Contributions, and begins the definition of Newly Eligible, including hiring or rehire and prior ineligibility.

nodes.title: Plan Eligibility and Contribution Definitions
nodes.summary: Defines Eligible Employees by payroll status, eligibility date, applicable plan requirements, Boeing 401(k) eligibility, and employer exclusions; defines Employees as Controlled Group common-law employees assigned to U.S. Executive Payroll. It also defines Extra Deferrals as elected pre-tax deferrals, Executive SSP+ Company Contributions as historical credits for periods before 2022, and Incentive Matching Contributions as those allocated under Section 4.3. The text also notes the 2022 default eligibility date.

nodes.title: 2.35 Newly Eligible
nodes.summary: Defines key Plan terms: “Newly Eligible” covers rehired or newly hired Employees meeting specified prior-plan eligibility and U.S.-payroll criteria; “Participant” covers eligible deferrers, Company Contribution recipients, and certain account holders; Participant Deferrals comprise Extra and Restoration Deferrals. It also defines Performance Awards, the Plan and its amendments, calendar-year Plan Year, PVP, pre-tax Restoration Deferrals, Restoration Matching Contributions, and historical Restoration SSP+ Company Contributions credited for periods before January 1, 2022.

nodes.title: Plan Definitions: Participants, Deferrals, and Contributions
nodes.summary: Defines Participant eligibility and account holders; Participant Deferrals as Extra and Restoration Deferrals; Performance Awards under Boeing incentive plans; the Plan and calendar-year Plan Year; and PVP. It also defines Restoration Deferrals as elected pre-tax Compensation, Restoration Matching Contributions credited under Section 4.1, and historic Restoration SSP+ Company Contributions for periods before January 1, 2022. The preceding text also specifies eligibility-related conditions involving 409A plan aggregation, distributions, and U.S.-dollar payroll.

nodes.title: Plan Definitions: Service and Deferrals
nodes.summary: Defines Restoration True-Up Contributions and Vested Performance Award Deferrals by reference to plan sections. Defines Separation from Service under Code section 409A, including an anticipated permanent service reduction below 50% of the prior 36-month average and an 80% controlled-group threshold. Defines Service as completed whole years under the Boeing Service Awards Program method. Specifies how Specified Employees are identified and when status applies, including the permitted 75-officer rule. Defines Unforeseeable Emergency under section 409A, as determined by the Administrator, and identifies US Executive Payroll levels and its former name.

summary: Defines plan accounts and historical contribution categories; the Administrator, Company, affiliates, subsidiaries, controlled group, Board, and related plans; compensation, pay, incentives, elections, deferrals, contribution types and credits, earnings, and eligibility dates. It also covers employees, newly eligible employees, participants and beneficiaries, plan years and awards, service and vesting-related terms, separation from service, specified employees, unforeseeable emergencies, payroll classifications, and applicable Code section 409A requirements.

title: ARTICLE III Participant Deferrals
summary: The article sets eligibility, limits, timing, and administration for annual and mid-year pre-tax Extra and Restoration Deferrals. Extra Deferrals may cover specified percentages of base pay, cash incentives, and performance awards without 401(a)(17) or 415(c) limits; Restoration Deferrals apply to base pay after those limits are reached and are capped by Boeing 401(k) contribution rates. Newly eligible employees may make limited mid-year elections, but not for incentives or awards. Elections may include distribution choices, generally carry over automatically, and follow deadlines and irrevocability rules; legacy elections continued on an evergreen basis. Elections may be cancelled for an unforeseeable emergency, and deferrals are credited when compensation would otherwise be paid.

title: ARTICLE IV Company Contributions

nodes.title: 4.1 Restoration Matching Contributions
nodes.summary: The Company credits a Restoration Matching Contribution for Base Pay deferrals made under a timely Restoration Deferral Election, calculated using the Participant’s Boeing 401(k) matching formula for the Plan Year. No match applies to Extra Deferral Election contributions. Eligibility requires a timely election under Section 3.3, and the match is credited when the related deferrals are credited. Distribution elections are addressed in Article VI.

nodes.title: 4.2 Restoration True-Up Contributions
nodes.summary: The Company may provide eligible employees a Restoration True-Up Contribution equal to the Boeing 401(k) true-up match calculated for the Plan Year (or the period before contributions stopped due to legal limits), less any actual Boeing 401(k) true-up match, as determined by the Committee. Payment requires Boeing 401(k) true-up eligibility and is generally barred if employment ends before the Plan Year’s last business day, except for specified retirement, Social Security-recognized disability, layoff, or death. Combined matching and restoration contributions cannot exceed 100% of the first 10% of eligible compensation contributed or credited to both plans. A Restoration Deferral Election is not required; distribution options are addressed in Article VI. Any contribution is credited when Boeing 401(k) true-up matches are made or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter.

nodes.title: 4.3 Incentive Matching Contributions
nodes.summary: Participants making Cash Incentive Deferrals may receive a Company Incentive Matching Contribution, calculated using the matching formula applicable under the Boeing 401(k) for that Plan Year. Eligibility requires a timely deferral election under Section 3.3. The match is credited when the related deferrals are credited; no match applies to incentives paid, or otherwise payable, after employment termination. Distribution elections are addressed in Article VI.

nodes.title: 4.4 Company Non-Elective Contributions (Component of the Executive Benefit)
nodes.summary: The Company may make non-elective contributions for eligible employees in amounts and under terms set by the Compensation Committee or delegates. For 2022 and 2023, contributions include 2% of Base Pay and Cash Incentive paid during the year, subject to a year-end employment requirement, with exceptions for qualifying retirement, Social Security Administration-determined disability, layoff, or death; post-termination incentives are excluded. For employees promoted onto the US Executive Payroll, eligible pre-promotion pay may be included under Administrator rules. Deferrals are not required for eligibility. Contributions are credited when made to the Boeing 401(k), if applicable, or as otherwise determined, as soon as administratively feasible; distribution elections are addressed in Article VI.

nodes.title: 4.5 DC SERP Contributions (Component of the Executive Benefit)
(i) Hired Between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019
nodes.summary: DC SERP contributions are available only to employees meeting specified eligibility conditions, but none are made for elected officers on or after January 1, 2020, or employees hired or promoted onto the US Executive Payroll on or after that date. For employees hired January 1, 2009–December 31, 2019, eligibility requires current US Executive Payroll level EL or EV (formerly E-1, E-2, or E-3), having been on that payroll at any E-1–E-5 level on December 31, 2019, not being an elected officer, and being ineligible for benefits under any Controlled Group defined benefit plan.

nodes.title: (ii) Hired Before January 1, 2009
nodes.summary: Employees hired before January 1, 2009 qualify under this rule only if they were on the US Executive Payroll at level E-1 through E-5 on December 31, 2019 and are not elected Company officers. Hire date generally means the most recent Company hire or rehire, subject to exceptions: direct returns from approved leave (including specified ULA or USA service) and uninterrupted Controlled Group transfers are not rehires; layoffs followed by rehire within six years generally are not rehires, except when the employee began retirement benefits during that period. Certain employees acquired through a merger or acquisition between September 30, 2008 and January 1, 2009 are deemed hired on or after January 1, 2009 for contributions from that date, with none payable earlier. Eligible employees participate during periods they meet the conditions, and participants may receive contributions as described in the Plan.

nodes.title: (i) Payroll Contributions
nodes.summary: Payroll contributions are credited when Base Pay and Cash Incentive would otherwise be payable, or as soon as administratively feasible. Participants hired from January 1, 2009 through December 31, 2019 receive a per-pay-period contribution based on pay and their level: 2% at EV (formerly E-2/E-3) or 4% at EL (formerly E-1); a level change is determined by the level on the period’s last day. Participants hired before January 1, 2009 receive a 5% credit, plus, if age 55 by the end of a Plan Year, 0.5% per whole year of qualifying Benefit Service determined as of January 1, 2016. This supplemental credit is limited to seven lifetime aggregate years, beginning on the latest of the specified dates: January 1, 2016, January 1 of the year age 55 is reached, or promotion to the US Executive Payroll. For both groups, pay counts only while on the US Executive Payroll, except qualifying Cash Incentive paid after termination but by the final regular paycheck.

nodes.title: (ii) One-Time Contribution
nodes.summary: Eligible employees first promoted during the Plan Year to EL/EV (formerly E-1 to E-3 before August 15, 2022) receive a one-time contribution equal to 2% of post-promotion base pay plus cash-incentive target value, multiplied by whole years of service since their most recent hire. It is credited at or soon after promotion, and no repeat contribution is allowed. Article V outlines vesting and forfeiture rules, cross-references other relevant provisions, and states Extra Deferral, Restoration, and generally Executive Benefit Accounts are always fully vested. The Administrator may forfeit post-2016 legacy Executive SSP+ contributions for specified felony misconduct or competitive activity during employment or within five years after termination.

The section establishes DC SERP eligibility for non-officer US Executive Payroll employees based on hire date, level, and defined-benefit-plan status, including special hire-date rules for leave, transfers, layoffs, and certain acquired employees. It describes participation periods and payroll contributions: 2% or 4% for 2009–2019 hires, and 5% plus a potentially age- and service-based supplemental credit for earlier hires, subject to limits. Newly promoted eligible employees may receive a one-time contribution. The section also addresses vesting and forfeiture, including exceptions for certain misconduct or competition.

nodes.title: Vesting and Forfeiture Rules
nodes.summary: Article V outlines vesting and forfeiture rules for Plan benefits, with related provisions on missing participants and improper credits, anti-assignment, the Plan’s unfunded status, and DCP Account forfeitures. Extra Deferral and Restoration Accounts are always 100% vested. Executive Benefit Accounts are also 100% vested, subject to Sections 5.5 and 5.6.

nodes.title: 5.5 Executive SSP+ Company Contribution Forfeiture Rules
nodes.summary: The Administrator may forfeit some or all legacy Executive SSP+ company contributions made from January 1, 2017, for conduct during employment or within five years after it ends: specified felony misconduct; competing with or acting adversely to Controlled Group businesses; improperly soliciting employees, representatives, or consultants; disparaging the group, its products, or employees; or misusing confidential information. Protected government communications and sworn testimony are exempt from the disparagement and confidentiality rules. The Administrator may seek legal or equitable recovery of amounts already paid; a court may narrow unenforceable provisions to their broadest enforceable scope. In appropriate cases, contributions tied to incentive awards subject to a cash-incentive clawback must also be reimbursed.

nodes.title: 5.6 DC SERP Vesting
nodes.summary: DC SERP payments are limited to vested amounts. Participants hired 2009–2019 generally vest fully after 36 consecutive months at specified executive payroll levels, death while employed, or qualifying executive layoff; those hired before 2009 have similar triggers, with death also requiring full PVP/BSS vesting before payments begin. Special age-and-service rules (55/10 or 62/1) provide full vesting of payroll contributions after 36 months and monthly pro-rata vesting of one-time contributions, without limiting death or layoff acceleration. Authorized absences count, but other breaks do not aggregate. Comparable uninterrupted ULA/USA executive service may count for direct transfers, subject to status limits. Separation or transfer can forfeit unvested payroll contributions; resumed service affects future one-time-contribution accruals, and each account component has separate vesting rules. Forfeitures are not reinstated; the text also references missing participants/improper credits, anti-assignment, and the plan’s unfunded status.

nodes.title: 5.7 DC SERP Forfeiture Rules
nodes.summary: The Administrator may, at its sole discretion, forfeit some or all of a participant’s DC SERP Account for specified conduct occurring during Controlled Group employment or within five years after termination: conviction of certain felonies or other harmful unlawful acts; competing with or acting adversely to the Controlled Group; improperly inducing its personnel or contractors to leave or breach contracts; disparaging the Controlled Group, its products, or employees; or, for contributions made from January 1, 2017, using or disclosing its confidential or proprietary information. Exceptions protect legally protected government communications and sworn testimony for the disparagement and confidentiality provisions. The Administrator may seek legal or equitable recovery of benefits already paid; a court may narrow unenforceable provisions to their enforceable scope. It must also require forfeiture or reimbursement, where appropriate, of account amounts tied to incentive awards recovered under a cash-incentive plan’s clawback.

summary: Covers Company restoration matching and true-up contributions, incentive matching, non-elective Executive Benefit contributions, and DC SERP eligibility, contribution amounts, crediting, and distribution references. It also addresses vesting and forfeiture, including account vesting rules, service and eligibility conditions, forfeiture for specified misconduct or competition, recovery of paid benefits, clawback-related reimbursement, and provisions on missing participants, improper credits, anti-assignment, and the Plan’s unfunded status.

title: ARTICLE VI Distributions

nodes.title: 6.1 Form and Timing of Distribution
nodes.summary: Article VI sets distribution rules for Extra Deferral, Restoration, Executive Benefit, and DCP accounts. Participants generally elect payment form and timing when first eligible; defaults are a lump sum in January after separation, with legacy Boeing elections preserved for certain Extra Deferrals. Benefits may be paid as a lump sum or 2–15 annual installments, valued at payment dates without subsequent earnings; installment balances of $10,000 or less are cashed out. Each account election may be changed once, subject to advance notice, a 12-month delay, and at least five additional years’ deferral; changes cannot extend payment beyond age 70½ and separation, or alter installments after they begin. Payments must begin by the January following separation and attainment of age 70½. Specified Employees face a six-month delay, with timing, valuation, installment, and death exceptions. Participants or beneficiaries may request emergency distributions from eligible accounts, limited to the amount reasonably needed; DC SERP funds are excluded.

nodes.title: 6.2 Death Benefits
nodes.summary: If a Participant dies before receiving the full Account balance, the remaining amount goes to the Beneficiary according to the Participant’s filed or deemed election, at the same time and in the same form as payments to the Participant would have been made, or as soon as administratively feasible after notice of death. If the Beneficiary later dies before receiving all amounts, unpaid amounts go to the Beneficiary’s designated beneficiary(ies), or, if none is designated or survives, to the Beneficiary’s estate in a lump sum as soon as administratively feasible.

nodes.title: 6.3 Rehires and Authorized Periods of Absence/Reduced Level of Services
nodes.summary: Section 6.3 explains payment rules when participants are rehired or continue working during an authorized absence or reduced-services period that constitutes a separation from service. Forfeited nonvested accounts are not restored upon rehire. After benefits begin, old-account installments continue despite rehire, while new-account payments follow the prior election and applicable separation/age rules; vested contributions made during qualifying absences are paid the following January. Before benefits begin, vested old and new accounts and absence-period contributions follow the earlier distribution election, including its payment timing and form, subject to election-change and specified-employee delay rules.

summary: Article VI governs distribution forms, timing, death benefits, and rehire or qualifying absence scenarios for eligible accounts. Participants generally elect a lump sum or 2–15 installments, subject to default rules, election-change limits, payment deadlines, specified-employee delays, and limited emergency distributions. Remaining balances pass to beneficiaries under the applicable election, then to successor beneficiaries or an estate. Rehire does not restore forfeitures; payment treatment for existing accounts and qualifying-period contributions depends on whether benefits have begun and on prior elections.

title: ARTICLE VII Accounts
key_items: 7.3 Investment Election Changes and Restrictions; 7.4 Missing Participants and Improper Credits
summary: The Administrator maintains a separate Account for each Participant and employment period, credits it with deferrals, company contributions and earnings, and reduces it for payments. A 2019 transfer moved specified participants’ Restoration Account balances to the SSP. Participants or beneficiaries may elect interest, Boeing Stock Fund, or other eligible investment-fund earnings; absent an election, interest applies. The text specifies how each method is valued, notes potential valuation adjustments, and explains rules for changing future investments and transferring balances, including a 30-day restriction on returning to the Boeing Stock Fund. Accounts may be forfeited or reduced for missing participants or recovery of improper credits, even when fully vested.

title: ARTICLE VIII Administration
summary: The Administrator administers the Plan, sets rules and interpretations, makes binding decisions on eligibility and benefits, may require electronic or telephone elections, and reports periodically to the Compensation Committee. Claims and appeals follow Boeing 401(k) procedures; for elected officers, the Compensation Committee reviews claims and appeals except potential forfeiture or reimbursement determinations under Sections 5.5 and 5.7, which remain with the Administrator. Subsequent legal action is subject to Section 10.8. The Board, Compensation Committee, Administrator, and their delegates may amend the Plan, including combining or transferring it or changing eligibility; only the Compensation Committee may change Company-provided benefit rates or amounts for US Executive Payroll employees. The Board may terminate the Plan. Amendment or termination preserves benefits at least at the amount payable upon immediate termination of employment, adjusted for subsequent Earnings Credits. Generally, distributions follow Article VI; Boeing may instead terminate the entire Plan and pay lump sums when permitted under Code Section 409A and related guidance.

title: ARTICLE X Miscellaneous

nodes.title: Plan Miscellaneous Provisions
nodes.summary: The Plan confers no employment rights or limits the employer’s ability to terminate employment. Benefits cannot be assigned or reached through legal process; prohibited attempts may lead to forfeiture, and Accounts may be reduced for unreimbursed taxes paid on a person’s behalf. The Plan is unfunded, with any related trust assets subject to general creditors and participants holding only unsecured creditor claims. The Administrator may delay or accelerate payments as permitted by Code section 409A; amounts determined currently taxable under that section are immediately distributed. Plan terms are to be construed to avoid 409A taxation.

nodes.title: Plan Construction, Claims, Taxes, and Payment Liability
nodes.summary: The Plan is interpreted under federal law and, where permitted, Illinois law; invalid provisions do not affect the rest. Benefit lawsuits must be filed within 180 days after an appeal decision or deadline, and participants consent to Illinois courts. The Company may withhold taxes, including specified FICA-related amounts, while participants remain responsible for excess personal tax liabilities. Benefit payments are solely the responsibility of the participant’s contributing employer unless another entity assumes liability; payments by others are made on that employer’s behalf.

nodes.title: Overpayment Recovery and Notices
nodes.summary: The Plan may recover excess benefit payments by offsetting future benefits as the Administrator determines, or through other reasonable actions if offset is impractical. Required or permitted notices and filings must be written and hand-delivered or sent by registered or certified mail to the Company’s headquarters, attention to its Secretary, or to the Participant’s or Beneficiary’s address on file, as applicable. Notices take effect upon delivery or, when mailed, on the postmark date shown on the registration or certification receipt.

summary: The Plan grants no employment rights; benefits are generally nonassignable and protected from legal process, with possible forfeiture or Account reductions for specified amounts. It is unfunded, leaving participants unsecured creditors, and permits payment timing adjustments consistent with Code section 409A, including immediate distribution of currently taxable amounts. The section covers governing law, severability, claim deadlines and Illinois courts, tax withholding and employer payment liability, recovery of overpayments, and written notice requirements and effective dates.

summary: Appendix B governs DCP accounts and participants as of December 31, 2021, and prevails over conflicting Plan terms. It notes when deferrals ended and limits on matching contributions, including legacy exceptions and treatment of prior matches. It sets forfeiture and reinstatement rules; identifies deferrals eligible or ineligible for investment diversification; explains distribution elections, defaults, changes, separate matching-contribution elections, installment options, and cross-references for age-70½ distributions, specified employees, emergencies, and rehires; and states beneficiary rules for death benefits.

title: CONSENT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM
summary: Deloitte & Touche consents to incorporating its January 27, 2023 reports on Boeing’s financial statements and internal-control effectiveness into specified Forms S-8 and S-3 registration statements. CEO David L. Calhoun and CFO Brian J. West certify their review of Boeing’s 2022 Form 10-K, the accuracy and fair presentation of its disclosures and financial information, and their responsibility for disclosure and financial-reporting controls, including their design, evaluation, and reporting of material changes, deficiencies, weaknesses, and relevant fraud. Both certifications are dated January 27, 2023.

West each certify under Section 906 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act that Boeing’s 2022 Form 10-K complies with applicable Securities Exchange Act reporting requirements and fairly presents the company’s financial condition and operating results in all material respects. Both certifications are dated January 27, 2023.
